accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum in England, Years 1 and 2 reading comprehension (check that the text makes sense as they read and correct inaccurate reading), Common Core RF.1.4c and RF.2.4c (use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary), Klingner and Vaughn's Collaborative Strategic Reading (click and clunk, fix-up strategies) and the EEF Key Stage 1 literacy guidance on teaching monitoring. The clue words famished, drenched, enormous, colossal, exhausted and ferocious are defined as the dictionary gives them.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: equating accurate decoding with understanding (prediction 1 and challenge item 1), skipping an unknown word (prediction 2), picking the line that holds the word instead of the clue line, choosing a fix-up that does not suit the clunk (read on when the whole page was lost), losing track of he, she and it (reread step), and over-marking sensible lines as clunks in the click-or-clunk check.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagclunk runs on a reader's running check of meaning: every story line is a row the child judges, the clue step needs the line that explains a word, the reread step needs the line that resolves a pronoun, and the check step marks a whole story click or clunk. flagcohe links sentences in a paragraph, flagnewword teaches new vocabulary and flaginfer draws inferences; none asks the child to notice a breakdown and repair it. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child can read every word of 'The rain was dry and hot' and still has to find it as the clunk, which is the discovery that decoding is not understanding. The clue step makes the meaning of famished come from the gobbled line, the reread step makes 'she' resolve from line 1, and the fix-up step matches each kind of breakdown to a strategy; the done messages only confirm.

predictions.evidence: Two locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, always' for whether reading every word means understanding, disproved by three stories of easy words that clunk; and 'Skip it and keep going' for an unknown word, before three words are solved only by reading on to the clue line.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with tagged wrong answers, each with its own correction: read every word so nothing to do, read faster, click because the words are easy, click because the line is short, ferocious as sleepy or soft against the roar and teeth clue, read on when the whole page was lost, carry on while lost, and Max or 'cannot tell' for who 'she' is.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK -0.7 against the family limit of 5.0 with lines like 'Stop at a clunk. Do not just keep going.' Adult text scores FK 8.6 against 10 and uses the precise terms comprehension monitoring, decoding, metacognitive, fix-up strategy, context clue, mental picture, self-correct and click and clunk.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph shows one clunk and one fix, each adult paragraph carries the standards, the method, named mistakes or the lab outline, and explanation overlap with every other lesson stays under the 12 percent limit.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360x640 in light and dark show each story line as a full-width row with wrapped 15 px text and a status light, the fix-up tiles in a 2 by 2 grid, and the Line 1 to Line 5 and Check buttons wrapping below; the five-line story fits without clipping. walk.cjs completed all five Show me tasks on desktop and iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme on desktop or iPhone and there were no console errors. Every canvas tap has a named button twin (each line button reads the full line in its aria-label, meanings and fix-ups are buttons), marks use an icon and a colour, and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. 'Line 1 makes sense. You can read it and it fits the story.'

sources: DfE (2013) National Curriculum in England: English programmes of study, Years 1 and 2 reading comprehension
Common Core State Standards ELA RF.1.4c and RF.2.4c
Klingner, J. K. and Vaughn, S. (1998) Using Collaborative Strategic Reading. Teaching Exceptional Children 30(6): click and clunk
EEF (2020) Improving Literacy in Key Stage 1: guidance report
